pr.title: Deliver watch events through Codex's native queue
pr.head: 1bfa3528c2e0e1659851cf4007b64da6f1c5e903

summary: Projector's watch daemon is one background process per machine. It polls GitHub for the pull requests that live agent sessions review or fix, and it writes each piece of new work, such as a new head or a reviewer's finding, as an event line to the session that owns it. In Claude Code, Projector's mod submits those lines as prompts. Before this change, Codex had no such adapter. The skills told a Codex session to run project watch stream, which prints events but cannot start a turn in an idle conversation.

This pull request adds a Codex adapter. Trusted Codex command hooks register the session with the daemon and acknowledge each delivery. The daemon sends events as a prompt with codex queue --thread <id> --message <batch> --resume, a CLI command that queues a message on a Codex thread and resumes the thread if it is not loaded. Claude Code's mod and the stream fallback keep working as before.

1. Register. The SessionStart hook runs project watch codex-hook. It records the session ID, the absolute codex executable, and the working directory in codex.json, with a 24-hour lease that each later hook renews.
  2. Queue. While the session is registered, the daemon writes its events to codex-events.json, each with a stable key that names the piece of work. A reminder of the same work in different words has the same key, so it never queues a second copy.
  3. Claim and send. On each tick, the daemon claims up to 8 KiB of events into one pending batch per session, and a pool of four worker threads runs codex queue with a 15-second timeout.
  4. Acknowledge. When Codex runs the queued prompt, the UserPromptSubmit hook matches its PROJECTOR WATCH <batch-id> marker, writes a receipt, and deletes the batch, so the next batch can go out.

The plan stays in-progress. Two live checks are still pending: the combined Codex queue-and-hook acknowledgment check in tests/codex_smoke.py, and the observation of real new-head and finding events in a live review and fix workflow.

cards.title: Batch states
cards.html:
StateMeansNext
preparedClaimed, not yet sentSent on the next tick
submittingcodex queue is runningRecovered as uncertain after a crash
queuedCodex accepted it (exit 0)Waits for acknowledgment, never resent
failedDefinite failureRetried after 30, 60, 120, 240, then 300 s
uncertainTimeout or crash mid-sendOnly project watch codex-retry resends it

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Registration: codex.json in the session's state folder, which binds the session to a Codex thread.
  • Lease: the 24-hour wall-clock expiry that host activity renews.
  • Key: the JSON identity of a piece of work, such as a repository, pull request, role, thread, and latest comment.
  • Receipt: codex-receipts/<batch-id>.json, which marks a batch consumed for 24 hours.
  • Transport: what delivers a session's events: mod, stream, or codex.

groups.title: The Codex delivery adapter
groups.kicker: One new module owns hooks, registration, durable batches, acknowledgment, and queue execution.
intro: src/projector/codex_watch.py holds everything that is specific to Codex. The daemon calls it to queue events and to send batches, and the CLI calls it to handle hook input. It uses only the standard library.

A batch moves through files in the session's folder, written atomically under the session's lock. prepare writes the pending batch before it removes the batch's keys from the queue. So when a crash interrupts a claim, recover finishes the claim by removing those keys again. A separate OS lock, codex-submit.lock, is held for the whole codex queue call, so that recovery can tell a send still running from one that crashed.

checks.text: Exit 0 from codex queue means Codex accepted the message, not that the thread ran it. A queued batch is therefore never resent automatically, and it holds back the session's next batch until the hook acknowledges it.

files.note: New module: registration, keyed queue, claim and recovery, acknowledgment, the push-command filter for PostToolUse, and the Dispatcher worker pool.

checks.text: append skips a key that is already in the queue or in the pending batch, so a reminder adds nothing while its batch waits. After the batch is acknowledged, a later reminder of standing work can queue the work again, as Claude's mod would.

eligible always passes MERGED, CLOSED, MISSING, and MOVED. Any other line must carry a key whose repository, number, and role match a subscription that is not excluded. prepare drops a queued item that fails this check.

Acknowledgment writes the receipt before it deletes the pending batch, and _send checks for the receipt before it records its result, so a result that arrives late cannot bring a consumed batch back. test_acknowledgment_racing_command_completion_cannot_resurrect_batch covers this, and it passes at this head.

An acknowledgment needs the prompt to equal the sent message exactly. If Codex changed the queued text, the batch would stay queued and the session would get no further batch. Only the pending live smoke test checks this against real Codex.

The submission lock is a flock on its own file descriptor, so the daemon's main thread sees a worker thread's send as running. A by-hand run of six definite failures gave retry delays of 30, 60, 120, 240, 300, and 300 seconds. The plan says 300 seconds for the fourth delay, and the review lists that as a suggestion.

groups.title: Daemon and CLI integration
groups.kicker: The existing daemon routes keyed events to the adapter and keeps a Codex session live under its lease.
intro: Each event producer in src/projector/watch.py now returns a codex_watch.Event, a string subclass that carries a key, so mod and stream sessions read exactly the text they read before. route_fix keys each item by its existing standing key, plus a revision: the head, latest comment ID, and body digest for a finding, or a body digest for a verdict or review. route_review keys a head by the head and reviewer, a RESPONDED event by the existing head-and-answer flag, and a stalled review by the stalled lock's identity.

A Codex session counts as live while its lease holds and it has subscriptions or pending events. Wall-clock expiry decides this, so the sleep forgiveness that keeps mod and stream sessions alive never extends a Codex lease. renew, take, and delivery refuse to let a second transport consume a session that Codex delivers to.

files.note: Keyed events from route_fix and route_review, Codex liveness in scan, the dispatcher tick, transport refusals, and deliveries in status.

checks.text: Codex sessions join live here, outside self.sessions, which is why forgive now skips names it has no record for.
The dispatcher ticks once per daemon turn, about once a second. For an idle registered session it reads files and starts no process. test_no_events_start_no_process_and_write_no_queue covers this.

files.note: Adds codex-hook, codex-retry, and disconnect, and prints each Codex delivery in watch status.

checks.text: The hook always exits 0 and prints Codex's hook JSON. A failure becomes a systemMessage of at most 200 characters, so a broken hook never blocks the user's turn.

groups.title: Codex hook packaging
groups.kicker: Codex loads its own command hooks. Claude Code keeps its TypeScript module.
intro: .codex-plugin/plugin.json now points Codex at codex-hooks/hooks.json, which runs the installed project watch codex-hook on five lifecycle events. Codex never reads hooks/hooks.json, which belongs to Claude's mod. The packaging test parses each hook command with the real CLI parser. The Claude panel test adds the isCollapsed prop that the current host requires, so the hooks type-check passes.

groups.title: Tests and the live harness
groups.kicker: Fake executables cover the adapter. An opt-in harness drives native Codex.
intro: tests/test_codex_watch.py runs a fake codex executable at the process boundary, uses a controlled clock, and drives the real daemon producers for the routing cases. tests/codex_smoke.py and tests/codex_smoke.mjs are not collected by unittest discover. They start a disposable local Codex server, create a test thread, restart the server to unload the thread, and check that the queued batch is acknowledged.

checks.text: The codex-fix session is subscribed here but never asserted on, and fix_folder is unused. The review suggests asserting that this session's queue stays empty.

groups.title: Skills, documentation, and the plan
groups.kicker: The shared skills learn the events: codex result, and the plan records what has been verified.
intro: The review-pr, fix-pr, review-repo, and implement skills add a row for events: codex, which means: start no stream. They also tell a Codex session to use the parent session ID that the hooks supply, and how to recover from a stuck delivery. docs/cli.md documents setup, the lease, status, retry, and switching to a stream. The plan's new § 7 records what has been built and verified, and what remains.
